title: Leader: the idea, the guest, sales
description: Leader track. Who your guest is, your own audience and a co-leader, sales against the cash plan, staying in touch with guests before arrival.

units.title: Who your guest is and what change they seek
Your own audience and a co-leader
Between the first payment and arrival

objectives.text: Describe one concrete guest and the change they are travelling for
Estimate the group by your own audience and write down the arrangements with a co-leader
Tie the pace of sales and payment options to the venue payment schedule
Place points of contact with guests from payment to arrival and turn a cancellation into a transfer

checks.question: Why does the course suggest writing the retreat description for one concrete guest?
options: So that only one type of person comes to the retreat
Because a person decides to come when they recognise themselves and their change in the description
Because advertising is cheaper that way
checks.explain: A week costing several thousand dollars is bought by someone who recognises themselves in the text. People do not apply a text "for everyone" to themselves (u1, "One person instead of 'everyone'").

checks.question: A leader invites a co-leader with a large audience. What does the course suggest basing the group plan on?
options: The co-leader's whole audience: it is bigger
Your own people, counting the partner's audience as a bonus and putting the arrangements in writing
The venue: it will find guests itself
checks.explain: People go away for a week with someone they trust. The group plan is built on your own audience, and arrangements with a co-leader are written down (u2).

checks.question: The monthly venue payment is 6,750 and a guest's first payment is 900. What follows?
options: One place sold a month is enough
First payments cannot cover a month without seven or eight new guests, so you need full payment, a bigger first payment or early sales
The venue payment can wait until there are sales
checks.explain: One or two places a month cover the payment only if the guest pays the whole price. With first payments you need more sales or other payment options (u3).

checks.question: A guest paid for a place, then stopped replying and is not paying the balance. What does the course suggest first?
options: Keep the first payment straight away under the terms
Talk: find out the reason and offer a transfer, passing the place on, or a different schedule
checks.explain: The reason for a cancellation is often ordinary and comes out in conversation. A transfer keeps the guest and the money with you (u4, "A cancellation is a conversation").
